title: The lead of a Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order cannot be changed
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  4. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card into the Unassigned column.
  5. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card within {Technician-A}'s column to above {Work-order-1}.
  6. Drag {Work-order-3}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column, then into the Unassigned column, then within {Technician-A}'s column to above {Work-order-1}.
  7. Drag {Work-order-4}'s card into {Technician-A}'s column, then drag it to a new place within the Unassigned column.
  8. Drag {Work-order-5}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column (click Keep shifts if asked).
  9. Drag {Work-order-6}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column (click Keep shifts if asked).
  10. Open {Work-order-2} and try to change Lead Technician on the work order page.
  11. Go back, click Tech View in the display switcher and do steps 3 to 7 again with the rows, then drag {Work-order-5}'s row into {Technician-B}'s group and drag {Work-order-6}'s row from {Technician-B}'s group back into {Technician-A}'s group.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 3, 4 and 6: {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} cannot be moved to {Technician-B} or to Unassigned: the card goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and the lead stays {Technician-A}. While {Work-order-2}'s card is over {Technician-B}'s column, the note "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" shows at the top of that column; for {Work-order-3} it reads "Paid · can’t be reassigned".
  • Steps 5 and 6: {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} can be moved within {Technician-A}'s column and keep their new place.
  • Step 7: {Work-order-4} cannot be moved out of Unassigned, but it can be reordered inside it.
  • Step 8: {Work-order-5} (Declined) cannot be moved to {Technician-B}: while its card is over {Technician-B}'s column the note “Declined · can’t be reassigned” shows at the top of that column, the card goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and the lead stays {Technician-A}.

    Step 9: {Work-order-6} (Complete) moves to {Technician-B} normally, with the message "{Work-order-6} assigned to {Technician-B}", with an "Undo" button.

  • Step 10: on the work order page the Lead Technician of {Work-order-2} cannot be changed either.
  • Step 11: Tech View follows the same rules for every move (the note shows at the top of {Technician-B}'s group). A change sent outside the screens is also refused by the server; this part cannot be checked by hand, so write "server refusal not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see. Imported work orders are checked in their own case.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R10, S4-N2, S4-N6, S4-R5 and Key decision: lead locked once Invoiced or Paid, read 19 Oct 2026. In version 48 (12 Oct 2026) S4-N2 dropped Imported from the locked statuses (Imported work orders now open in List only); the Invoiced and Paid rules this case checks are unchanged, so the expected results are unchanged. Review Decisions DR-37 (Declined and Complete move freely) was replaced in PRD version 82 (29 Oct 2026, SV-11902): Declined now locks the lead technician; Complete still moves freely. PO answer to engineering, Sasha Grosman 24 Sep 2026 (Invoiced/Paid reorder within their technician or within Unassigned). In versions 66 to 68 (19 Oct 2026) the Invoiced or Paid rule was extended to Unassign and Undo, S4-N6 gave the drag note the design's words, and the message after a move became "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo; the results of steps 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 11 follow. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message after a lead change reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

PRD version 82 (29 Oct 2026, SV-11902; read 29 Oct 2026): a Declined work order now locks its lead technician exactly like an Invoiced or Paid one (S4-N2, S4-N6, S4-N7, S4-R32); Complete work orders still move freely. The results of steps 8 and 11 follow, and the quotes below are from version 82. The Declined behaviour was seen on the QA branch sv11902 (build v26.43.3-74314c9) on 29 Oct 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R10: “Enforce the prohibited-status rule in S4-N2 on every lead-change path, including requests that bypass interface controls.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Declined, Invoiced or Paid status. A Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today. The lock follows the work order’s status at the moment of the change: a work order is Declined only while every one of its lines is declined, so when a line is re-approved or a new line is added and the work order becomes Estimate or Approved, its lead can change again. Only the work order’s own status counts: a declined line on a work order in any other status does not lock it.”
  • S4-N6: “On a Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Declined · can’t be reassigned”, “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, in the design’s format. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • Key decision: lead locked once Invoiced or Paid: “Lead technician cannot be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid. This is a product rule, not only a screen rule, so it must hold on every path that changes the lead technician — board drag, the lead technician dialog, Unassign, Undo, and the work order detail page.”
